critic-002

objections.requirement: Reconcile the method description with its parameters. The text says 'box-clipped MLE under a uniform prior', while the params are estimator='mode', tikhonov=0.0 and posterior_samples=128. Confirm that posterior_samples is unused for the mode estimator. Confirm whether clipping is projection after the optimiser runs or a bounded optimiser in log space.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Report forward-evaluation usage for the physics arm on validation (750 rows × 3 starts × 25 iterations plus Jacobian evaluations) and confirm it stays within max_forward_evals=3,000,000.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Make the per-target diagnostics actually compare arms. S-Q1-02.per_target_physics_et and S-Q1-02.per_target_physics_mlp contain identical, treatment-only per_target_rel_l2 values and no control per-target rel_l2. Report control and treatment per-target rel_l2 side by side, with per-target paired intervals. The edge segments (targets 1 and 4, RMSE about 0.035) are notably worse than the interior segments; the synthesis should say whether the physics advantage holds for each segment.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Use more replicates. Two seeds per data-driven control give a one-degree-of-freedom spread estimate, and n_bootstrap=200 is thin for interval endpoints. Use at least 3–5 seeds and at least 1000 bootstrap resamples. Given the current lower bounds (0.27 and 0.73 against a 0.10 margin), this is unlikely to flip either claim, but it is needed for a credible seed-variance term.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Keep the synthesis within scope. The controls are fixed-configuration and untuned: extra_trees with max_features=0.5, and a 256x256 GELU MLP trained for 150 epochs. The test is an inverse-crime setting in which the inversion uses the exact generator and noise model, and the comparison is simulator access versus 3000 rows, not an equal-information comparison. Any conclusion must not generalise to 'physics methods outperform data-driven methods'. It must not imply robustness to model misspecification or transfer to the held-out test or stress splits.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Correct the completion bookkeeping. completion_fraction=1.0 and completed_work=5/5 are reported alongside status='incomplete', missing_diagnostics, and completed_claim_work=0/2. The completion metric should reflect the missing required diagnostics, so downstream synthesis does not treat the study as finished.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Document that the training observations carry the same noise process (i.i.d. N(0, 0.001²) per sensor) as the validation observations. Without this, part of the control gap could come from a train/validation noise mismatch rather than from simulator access.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Missing evidence: evidence_ids and verdicts are empty and status is 'planned'. C-Q2-1 cannot be evaluated until both required arms (S-Q2-01.mode, S-Q2-01.mean) have run on the same validation rows. Both required diagnostics (S-Q2-01.paired_mean_mode, S-Q2-01.per_target_mean_mode) must also be produced, with artifacts traceable to the val split fingerprint edfcc32d…7c0543.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Estimator definition (implementation): specify how 'posterior mean' is computed from the 128 posterior samples. Name the sampler (importance sampling from a Laplace/Gaussian proposal at the mode, MCMC, or other), the proposal, and the weighting. The mean must be taken in original conductivity space, i.e. E[k|y], not exp(E[log k|y]). Squared-error rel_l2 is minimized in expectation by the former. The latter is a geometric-mean/median-type estimator and would not test the stated hypothesis.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Prior/Jacobian correctness: the contract prior is i.i.d. uniform on [0.5, 2.0] in k, but sampling runs in log space (transform='log'). The target density in log k must include the Jacobian term (∝ k, i.e. +log k in the log-density) and must be truncated to [log 0.5, log 2]. If this is omitted, the sampler targets a log-uniform prior and the result is the posterior mean under the wrong prior. Verify this in code and with a unit test.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Likelihood correctness: the posterior must use additive i.i.d. Gaussian noise with sigma = 0.001 on all 80 features (4 sensors at indices [5,15,25,35] × 20 time samples). The same forward operator (40-point explicit FD, 200 steps, Dirichlet BCs, known Gaussian initial condition at x = 0.5) and the same time-subsampling as the data generator must be used. A mis-scaled sigma (e.g. one inflated by noise augmentation) changes posterior width and directly biases the mean-versus-mode gap.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Implementation verification (required by the claim): before reading validation results, validate the posterior-mean code on a toy case with a known posterior. Two options are a linear-Gaussian surrogate with an analytic mean, or a 1-parameter case checked by dense quadrature. Report the agreement. Also report importance-weight effective sample size (or MCMC diagnostics) per row. Rows with ESS near 1 make the 'mean' effectively equal to a single sample or the mode.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Matched control: confirm the mean arm reuses exactly the same multistart optimization as the mode arm. That means same 3 starts, 25 iterations, seed 0, and identical selected optimum per row, with only the final estimator differing. Also confirm the mode arm reproduces the values exported from S-Q1-03 bit-for-bit, or by a stated tolerance. A re-run that diverges from the S-Q1-03 export breaks the claimed 'identical settings' pairing.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Compute asymmetry: the mean arm spends at least 128 extra forward evaluations per row beyond the mode arm. Report forward-eval counts per arm. Confirm total usage across validation rows stays within max_forward_evals = 3,000,000, including multistart, gradient evaluations (adjoint or finite-difference) and posterior sampling. State whether the budget difference is accepted as part of the intervention.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Uncertainty specification: pre-register the paired bootstrap before looking at results. Fix the statistic as 1 − rel_l2(mean)/rel_l2(mode), with both global-Frobenius norms recomputed on the same resampled rows each replicate. Fix the number of replicates (≥ 2000), the interval method (percentile or BCa), the one-sided 95% lower bound, and the bootstrap RNG seed. The claim passes only if that lower bound is ≥ 0.02.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Unaccounted Monte Carlo variability: row-resampling uncertainty ignores sampler noise from the 128 posterior samples drawn under a single seed. Report the per-row Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior-mean estimate, or re-run the sampler with several seeds. This shows whether the improvement is stable relative to the 2% margin. Otherwise narrow the claim's scope explicitly to seed 0.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Optimizer convergence: 25 iterations with 3 starts may leave the mode arm unconverged on some rows. That would handicap the control and inflate the apparent benefit of averaging. Report per-row final objective, gradient norm or step size, the fraction of rows at a bound (clipping active), and the cross-start spread for both arms.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Numerical stability: explicit FD with k up to 2.0 must satisfy dt·k_max/dx² ≤ 0.5 for all parameters that posterior samples or optimizer iterates can reach. Specify the handling of NaN/unstable forward solves. Any failed rows must be identical across arms and reported, not silently dropped; dropping rows asymmetrically would bias the paired comparison.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Per-target diagnostic interpretation: report the rel_l2/RMSE difference per segment with paired uncertainty. A pooled 2% gain could be driven entirely by one poorly observed segment where the posterior is wide or bound-truncated. Link per-target gains to segment-sensor geometry rather than presenting them as a uniform improvement.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Training data isolation: state whether the training split (3000 rows, augmentation, scaler, PCA) influences either physics arm, e.g. via initialization or noise estimates. If it does, both arms must use it identically. Test and stress observations must not be used for any choice of sampler, proposal scale, sample count or margin.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Synthesis scope: the claim text must keep its stated limits. These are inverse-crime data (same simulator generated and inverts), single seed, row-resampling uncertainty only, and the validation split. It must not assert Bayes-optimality or global identifiability; per diagnostic_limits, any Fisher/Laplace argument is local only. Rename 'mode (MLE)' as 'box-clipped MLE (= MAP under the uniform prior with tikhonov = 0)' for precision.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Prior plausibility of the effect: with sigma = 0.001, posteriors may be very concentrated for well-observed segments, so mean ≈ mode there. A ≥ 2% pooled gain would then depend on weakly identified or boundary-truncated rows. Report posterior standard deviation (or Laplace width) per target alongside the result. A null outcome is then interpretable rather than attributed to implementation failure.
objections.author: critic-002

messages.author: researcher-003
messages.question: Q-1
messages.text: Design rationale, not a result: no evidence exists yet, so every claim here is an untested hypothesis. The forward map is deterministic, has 4 parameters, and the noise is small (sigma=1e-3). Under those conditions, likelihood-based fitting through the simulator should approach the local noise floor. Regressors trained on 3000 prior samples face an 80-dimensional input and are limited by sample density. The margin is a 10% relative improvement, not 'any' improvement, so that a 'substantially lower' finding means something. Both strong library controls use log targets, matching the physics log transform, so the comparison isolates estimator class rather than parameterization. Ridge is an optional linear floor. The physics settings (25 iters, 3 starts) are chosen to fit the 760 s budget, and forward-eval usage should stay far below the 3M cap. If physics wins by less than the margin, or the paired diagnostic shows a heavy tail of multistart failures, the next step is the hybrid initializer from Q-2 rather than more starts. The per-target diagnostic is collected now so Q-3 can reuse it. The claims are not certified here; they need the executed paired diagnostics and implementation verification.

interpretation.interpretation: Task task-001 (artifact resu-00129, specialist-004) did not produce any diagnostic output. The task status is 'incomplete' and the result status is 'unsupported', with the stated uncertainty 'no executable study returned'. The run used 38.0 s of a 60 s limit. No numbers exist for any of the requested quantities: (a) chi2(estimate) vs chi2(truth) optimizer-failure fraction and chi2(estimate)/80 distribution, (b) per-target bound-hit fractions at 0.5 / 2.0, (c) non-finite and fallback counts, (d) median Cramér–Rao standard deviations from the local Fisher information at true k. Q-1 therefore gets no new evidence on optimizer adequacy or clipping for the physics arm of S-Q1-02 (resu-00118, val_pred at exp-0007). Any earlier interpretation of that arm's errors as optimizer failure, bound clipping, or intrinsic non-identifiability stays unresolved by this task. The null result is not evidence for or against any of these hypotheses. The failure is in execution or tooling: no study was returned. That differs from a finding that the diagnostic is infeasible. The request was within budget (about 3,300 forward evals) and used validation rows only. Suggested next step: resubmit as an executable script using batched forward calls, or split the request into (a–c), which need only the stored predictions plus 2 evals per row, and (d), which runs on 200 rows.

messages.author: researcher-003
messages.question: Q-1
messages.text:
Researcher interpretation (unverified; no claim is certified). S-Q1-02 executed all 5 required arms on the same 750 validation rows (row_hash 260db427…). Both claims are still inconclusive. The only unmet requirements are the two seed diagnostics, S-Q1-02.paired_et_seed and S-Q1-02.paired_mlp_seed. They failed with 'paired rows/seed/fidelity differ' because they pair arms with different seeds, which the harness's paired analysis does not allow. This is a design error on my part, not a result.

Measured values (validation rel_l2, original k scale per the harness metric):
- physics: 0.01933
- extra_trees: 0.07741 (s0), 0.07711 (s1)
- torch_mlp: 0.02805 (s0), 0.03016 (s1)
- ridge (context only, per obj-015): 0.06603

Paired bootstrap results (200 resamples, row sampling only, conditional on fitted models):
- physics vs ET s0: relative improvement 0.750, 95% interval [0.728, 0.770] (resu-00120).
- physics vs MLP s0: relative improvement 0.311, 95% interval [0.272, 0.352] (resu-00121).
- Both lower bounds exceed the 0.10 margin.

Under the pre-registered conservative rule (each claim must hold against the better-scoring control seed):
- The better MLP seed is s0, which is already the paired control.
- For ET, the better seed is s1. The point estimate against it is 1 − 0.01933/0.07711 ≈ 0.749. That figure is my arithmetic, not a paired artifact.

Caveats that remain open:
1. Seed variance is unestimated with 2 seeds (obj-020), and the physics arm is single-seed (obj-021).
2. torch_mlp_s1 (resu-00110) and ridge (resu-00111) are cache reuses of earlier experiments (exp-0005, exp-0006); torch_mlp_s1 ran on cpu. That the seed-1 intervention was actually applied is not verified (intervention_verified=false on all arms).
3. Optimizer adequacy is not yet shown (obj-018). last_iters=25 equals the cap on at least the last row, and no per-row NLL(estimate) vs NLL(truth) or convergence data exists.
4. Boundary-clipping fractions are not reported (obj-025).
5. n_bootstrap=200 is small for the interval tails.

Partial evidence on earlier objections:
- Inverse-crime and fidelity (obj-002): fit_report shows residual_std_at_truth 0.000995 ≈ sigma, model_mismatch=false, and last chi2/dof 0.963. This points to an exact forward model, so any win must be framed as simulator access in an inverse-crime setting (obj-030).
- Forward-eval budget (obj-023): 174,077 total evals (about 232 per row plus 200 in fit), against a 3,000,000 cap.
- Compute is not matched (obj-010): physics predicts in 14.95 s at about 19.9 ms per row; MLP takes 10.2 s to fit and about 0.016 ms per row to predict.
- Uncertainty calibration: 1σ/2σ coverage is 0.702/0.957, close to nominal.

Per-target pattern, relevant to Q-3 and obj-026:
- physics per-target rel_l2: [0.0268, 0.0060, 0.0050, 0.0263]. The outer segments k1 and k4 are about 4–5× worse than the central ones.
- ET and MLP show the same outer/inner ordering.
- Physics is lower than ET and MLP on every target (per-target RMSE in resu-00120/121). The aggregate win is therefore not driven only by the central segments, though it is smallest in relative terms for MLP on k4 (0.0350 vs 0.0448 RMSE).
- Ridge's central-segment errors (0.0128, 0.0113) beat both nonlinear baselines there. This suggests the central map is close to linear, and that the baseline weakness is concentrated in the outer segments.

Next step: revise to S-Q1-03 so that the seed requirement is satisfiable through matched-seed pairs. This adds a physics seed-1 arm, which also addresses obj-021, at an estimated ~17 s. In parallel, commission the optimizer-adequacy and clipping diagnostic.

interpretation.interpretation: Task-002 (PART A of the optimizer-adequacy diagnostic, artifact resu-00244, specialist-005) returned no usable result: status 'incomplete', result status 'unsupported', with the stated uncertainty 'no executable study returned'. It ran for 10.6 s against a 60 s limit. No forward evaluations are reported, and no chi2 values, fractions, quantiles, row indices, boundary-hit fractions, non-finite or fallback counts, or val_idx alignment results were produced. This is the second consecutive failure: it resubmits task-001 (a)-(c), which also returned no executable output. So this artifact provides no evidence for or against optimizer adequacy for the S-Q1-03 physics arms resu-00228 (seed 0, exp-0020) and resu-00230 (seed 1, exp-0021). Specifically, it cannot tell us whether estimates have higher chi2 than the true k (optimizer failure versus model or identifiability limits), whether estimates sit on the 0.5/2.0 bounds, whether the 1.25 prior-centre fallback was triggered, or whether exp-0017/0018/0020-0023 are row-aligned. None of these should be inferred from this result. The early return well inside the time limit suggests the failure is in the adapter or script setup, for example the context.forward or val_pred loading path, rather than the 3,000-eval budget. That is an inference, not something the artifact shows. Q-1 claims that depend on PART A remain unsupported until a resubmission returns executable output. The resubmission should probably be split further, for example (e) the alignment check alone, then a single arm's (a1)-(c).

No interpretable evidence for Q-1. Task task-003 (artifact resu-00248, specialist-006 under researcher-003) is marked incomplete. Its result status is 'unsupported', with the stated uncertainty 'no executable study returned'. It ended after about 10.8 s, well under the 60 s limit, so it was not cut off by the time limit; it simply produced no executable study. The original request is redacted, so it is not possible to tell what was being tested or to infer any finding. This artifact cannot support or refute any claim about Q-1. A new or retried execution that returns a runnable study and its outputs is needed before Q-1 can be interpreted.

Task task-004 (artifact resu-00252, specialist-007) returned no usable result: status 'incomplete', result status 'unsupported', and the only recorded uncertainty is 'no executable study returned'. It ran for about 25.3 s of a 60 s limit, so the time limit does not explain the failure. No Jacobian, Fisher matrix, CR_sd_log median/p90, condition number, (k1,k4)/(k2,k3) correlation, or CRLB-based rel_l2 reference was produced. The evidence therefore says nothing about local Fisher sensitivity for Q-3. It does not support or weaken objection 044, and it does not address the mirror-symmetry concern in objection 013. Absence of output must not be read as evidence of non-identifiability or of good conditioning. The failure may mean context.jacobian was unavailable and the central-difference fallback was never run, but the record does not show this. Q-1 remains open on this axis. A rerun is needed that confirms an executable path (jacobian or the fallback of 8+1 evals per row, about 1,800 evals for 200 rows, which exactly matches the budget). Any rerun results should be scoped as local sensitivity under the Gaussian noise model, not global identifiability.

specialist-004.question:
Optimizer-adequacy and clipping diagnostic for the physics arm of S-Q1-02 (resu-00118, val_pred at exp-0007), on the same 750 validation rows (row_hash 260db427…). For every row, compute and report:
(a) chi2(estimate) = sum of squared residuals / sigma^2 at the predicted k, and chi2(truth) at the true k, using the context forward model with batched calls. Report the fraction of rows where chi2(estimate) > chi2(truth) + 1e-6, i.e. optimizer failures, and the distribution of chi2(estimate)/80.
(b) The per-target fraction of estimates within 1e-6 of the bounds 0.5 or 2.0.
(c) The count of non-finite estimates and the count of rows that used any fallback.
(d) The local Fisher information J^T J / sigma^2 in log-k at the true k, for the first 200 rows. Report median per-target Cramér–Rao standard deviations, scoped as local sensitivity only per diagnostic_limits.
Use only validation rows and no training targets. Budget: at most 2 forward evals per row for (a) and 9 per row for a central-difference Jacobian in (d), about 3,300 evals in total.

specialist-005.question: PART A of the optimizer-adequacy diagnostic. This resubmits task-001 (a)-(c), which returned no executable output; keep it to one small script. Inputs: the S-Q1-03 physics arms resu-00228 (seed 0, val_pred at exp-0020) and resu-00230 (seed 1, val_pred at exp-0021), the 750 validation rows (row_hash 260db427..., fingerprint edfcc32d...), and the validation observations and targets. For each arm, run one batched context.forward call on the (750,4) predicted k and one on the (750,4) true k, then compute per row chi2 = sum((y_obs - forward)^2) / 0.001^2. Report: (a1) the fraction of rows with chi2(est) > chi2(truth) + 1e-6, plus that fraction restricted to rows where the gap exceeds 1.0 and 10.0; (a2) quantiles p10/p50/p90/p99/max of chi2(est)/80 and chi2(truth)/80; (a3) the indices of the 10 rows with the largest chi2(est) - chi2(truth), together with their per-sample squared error; (b) the per-target fraction of estimates within 1e-6 of 0.5 or 2.0, and the same for the true k; (c) the count of non-finite estimates and the count of rows equal to the prior-centre fallback 1.25 in all four coordinates; (e) a row-alignment check confirming that the val_idx arrays of exp-0020, exp-0021, exp-0022, exp-0023, exp-0017 and exp-0018 are elementwise identical. Use no training targets. Budget is 4 x 750 = 3,000 forward evals. Return a JSON dict of the numbers only.

specialist-006.question: Forward-model fidelity and stability check, for objections 036 and 037. (1) For the first 20 validation rows, compute r = y_obs - context.forward(true_k) and report the per-row RMS(r), the overall mean and std of r, and a Shapiro or KS p-value against N(0, 0.001^2). An exact forward model gives RMS about 1e-3 and mean about 0. (2) From context.facts or the solver object, report dx, dt, the number of steps, the final time, the sensor grid indices, the observation time indices and the flatten order (sensor-major or time-major) that produce the 80 features. Also report the face-averaging rule for k at segment interfaces (harmonic or arithmetic) and the segment-to-grid mapping. (3) Report r_max = dt * 2.0 / dx^2 and state whether it is <= 0.5. (4) Report whether context.clip or the physics solver projects every iterate onto [0.5, 2.0] before calling forward, or only the final estimate. Test this by calling forward on k = [2.2, 2.2, 2.2, 2.2] and on k = [0.45, ...], and report whether the outputs are finite and whether they equal forward(clip(k)). Budget: at most 30 forward evals. Return numbers and booleans only.

specialist-007.question: PART B (task-001 (d)), local Fisher sensitivity for Q-3 and objection 044, using the first 200 validation rows. Call context.jacobian(theta=true_k, h=1e-3, transform='log') batched over rows; if it is unavailable, use a central difference in log k with 8 evals per row plus 1 base eval. Compute F = J^T J / 0.001^2 and CR_sd_log = sqrt(diag(F^-1)). Report the median and p90 of CR_sd_log per target, the median of CR_sd in k units (k * CR_sd_log), the median condition number of F, and the median correlation from F^-1 for the pairs (k1,k4) and (k2,k3), which bears on the mirror-symmetry concern in objection 013. Also report a CRLB-based reference rel_l2 = sqrt(sum_rows sum_targets (k * CR_sd_log)^2) / ||k||_F over these 200 rows, for interpretation only. Scope everything as local sensitivity under the Gaussian noise model per diagnostic_limits, not as global identifiability. Budget: at most 1,800 forward evals.

objections.requirement: Forward-evaluation budget accounting: before running, state the expected forward-solve count for the physics arm as N_val × multistart (3) × iters (25) × solves per iteration (Jacobian or finite-difference cost for 4 parameters plus line search), plus any cost from posterior_samples=128. Show that the total is at most 3,000,000. Log the actual count per row and in total. A run that exceeds the budget, or that truncates silently to stay under it, invalidates both claims.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Forward-model fidelity and inverse-crime disclosure: verify that the physics arm's forward operator matches the data generator in every respect: 40-point grid, 200 explicit steps, Dirichlet BCs, Gaussian IC at x=0.5, sensor indices [5,15,25,35], and the exact time indices behind the 80 features. Show that reproducing training rows from their true k gives residual RMS ≈ sigma = 0.001. If the operator is identical to the generator, the synthesis must state that the advantage is measured under zero model misspecification (inverse crime) and must not be generalized beyond that.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Numerical stability of the explicit scheme: confirm the CFL condition dt ≤ dx²/(2·k_max) holds for k up to 2.0, the upper bound. It must also hold for any iterate the optimizer can visit, so either the box constraint has to be enforced inside the solver or the log-space iterates have to be clipped. If the scheme goes unstable, the objective becomes non-finite or misleading and the optimizer can diverge silently.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Definition of the 'MAP' estimator: with a uniform prior and tikhonov=0.0, the k-space MAP equals the box-constrained MLE. Optimizing in log space while calling the result MAP either adds the log-Jacobian term (which shifts the mode toward small k) or omits it (which makes it an MLE). State which objective is optimized, how the [0.5, 2.0] bounds are enforced (projection, barrier, or clipping after the fact), and what estimator='mode' together with posterior_samples=128 actually computes. The claim text must match the implemented estimator.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Implementation verification for the physics arm, which both claims require: (a) a gradient check (adjoint or autodiff against finite differences) at random prior draws; (b) noiseless and noisy recovery tests on rows drawn from the training split with known truth; (c) convergence diagnostics for each validation row, namely the final misfit compared with the expected chi-square level (about 80·sigma²), the gradient norm, and how many of the 3 starts reached the best basin. Rows whose best misfit is well above the noise floor must be reported as optimization failures.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Failure and row-retention policy: every validation row must be scored. Rows where the physics solver fails, returns NaN, or hits the budget cannot be dropped. Pre-register a fallback, such as the prior mean or the best start found, and report how many rows used it.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Uncertainty quantification matched to the metric and margin: rel_l2 is a global Frobenius ratio, not a mean of per-row values, so use a paired bootstrap over validation rows that recomputes both arms' global rel_l2 in each resample. Test the claim as follows: the upper confidence bound of rel_l2_phys / rel_l2_ctrl must be at most 0.9. Pre-register the confidence level, the number of bootstrap resamples, and the bootstrap seed. Each of C-Q1-1 and C-Q1-2 must pass separately; they are evaluated as an intersection and are not pooled.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Control seed variance: each control is run with a single seed (seed=0). torch_mlp in particular has meaningful variance across initialization and batch order. Run at least 3–5 seeds per control, or report the seed-to-seed spread and fold it into the uncertainty, so that a margin result cannot come from one unlucky control seed. Any randomness in the physics multistart initialization should also be seeded and reported.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Control strength versus the claim wording: the question says 'best purely data-driven library regressors', but the controls use fixed, untuned hyperparameters: MLP for 150 epochs with no early stopping, and ET with defaults. Either tune the controls with a matched budget using cross-validation inside the training split only, never the validation split, or drop the word 'best' and describe the controls as fixed-configuration baselines.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Information asymmetry in the matched comparison: the physics arm uses privileged knowledge (exact PDE, IC, BCs, noise sigma) and a per-row compute budget that the data-driven arms do not have. These factors are allowed to vary, but the synthesis must say the comparison is between access to a simulator and 3,000 training rows. It must not be presented as an algorithmic comparison under equal information. Report wall-clock time and compute for each arm.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Target-scale handling: confirm that the library arms' log target transform is inverted with exp before scoring, and that every arm is scored on the original k scale with the same rel_l2 implementation applied to the same validation rows, identified by the val fingerprint.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Noise-augmentation ambiguity: transform_order lists observation_noise_augmentation, but no arm specifies noise_scale or the number of copies. State explicitly whether augmentation is used. If the controls use it, report its configuration. If they do not, record that.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Per-target and identifiability reporting: rel_l2 is weighted toward large k values and can hide poor recovery of weakly sensed segments. The outer segments sit near the Dirichlet boundaries, where the pulse signal decays. Also, the pulse and the sensor layout are nearly mirror-symmetric about the rod centre (indices 5/35, 15/25 on a 40-point grid). Run the per_target diagnostic, for example per-target RMSE and R², for all three arms, not only physics against MLP. Inspect for near-mirror confusions, i.e. k1↔k4 and k2↔k3. Local Fisher analysis may support this but is not a global identifiability result.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Held-out discipline: no test-split or stress observations may inform choices of iters, multistart count, fallback policy, control tuning, or margin. Record the test fingerprint as unopened at the time the verdict is decided.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Optional ridge baseline: if the ridge arm is run, report it as context only. It cannot stand in for a required control, and its result must not be used to frame either claim.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Missing evidence: evidence_ids is empty and the study status is 'planned'. No verdict on C-Q1-1 or C-Q1-2 can be issued until all three required arms and both paired diagnostics (S-Q1-01.paired_et, S-Q1-01.paired_mlp) have produced logged artifacts and the implementation-verification items above are attached.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Implementation verification (required by both claims): show that the physics arm's forward operator matches the data generator. It must use the same 40-point grid, 200 explicit steps, dt, Gaussian IC at x=0.5, Dirichlet BCs, sensor indices [5,15,25,35] and the exact time-subsampling that yields the 80 features (4 sensors x 20 times?). Test: for a sample of validation rows, simulate at the true theta and check that residuals against the observations are consistent with N(0, 0.001^2), e.g. a chi-square of about 80 per row. Without this check, 'zero misspecification' is asserted, not verified.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Optimizer adequacy check for 25 iterations x 3 starts. For each validation row, report the negative log-likelihood at the estimate versus at the true theta. Rows where NLL(estimate) > NLL(truth) are optimizer failures, not inherent error. Also report the fraction of such rows, the fraction of NaN or non-converged rows, and how they are handled. No row may be dropped; failures must be scored.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Pre-specify the uncertainty procedure for an at_least_better claim with margin 0.1 on rel_l2, which is a global Frobenius ratio and not a mean of per-row values. Use a paired bootstrap over validation rows of the ratio R = rel_l2(physics) / rel_l2(control), recomputing both Frobenius norms within each resample. The decision rule must be fixed in advance, e.g. upper 95% bound of R < 0.9. State the validation row count.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: C-Q1-2 states that MLP seed-to-seed spread is folded into the uncertainty, but only two seeds (0, 1) exist. Two seeds cannot estimate a spread. Either add seeds (at least 5) or define a conservative rule, e.g. the claim must hold against the better of the seeds, and state that the seed variance is unestimated. The same limitation applies to the extra_trees seed diagnostic.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The physics arm is single-seed, yet multistart initialisation is stochastic. Either show that the starts are deterministic, or run at least one extra physics seed so that the treatment's own variability is part of the uncertainty, not just the controls'.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Metric scale: all arms use log targets or log-space estimation. Verify that rel_l2, rmse and r2 are computed on conductivity in original units after exp back-transform, with identical code for every arm. Note that exp of a log-space estimate is not a mean-squared-error-optimal estimate in raw space.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Forward-evaluation budget accounting. Report the total number of forward solves the physics arm uses: validation rows x 3 starts x 25 iterations x evaluations per iteration, including finite-difference or adjoint gradient cost. Show the total is at most 3,000,000. If the budget binds, iterations or starts cannot be silently truncated.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Parameter inconsistency in the physics arm: estimator='mode' with posterior_samples=128, and tikhonov=0. State whether posterior samples are drawn and unused, or whether they affect the reported point estimate. Note that under rel_l2 (a squared-error metric) the posterior mean, not the MAP/MLE, is the risk-optimal estimator. A loss to the baselines is therefore not evidence that physics information is weak.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Box-clipping bias. Report the fraction of estimates on or clipped to the bounds 0.5 or 2.0, per target. Clipping changes the estimator relative to an unconstrained MLE, and the claim text should describe it as clipped MLE.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Identifiability per segment. With a pulse centred at 0.5 and Dirichlet ends, the outer segments (sensors 5 and 35) may receive little signal relative to sigma=0.001 within the window. The required per-target diagnostics should be read together with a local Fisher or sensitivity summary, scoped as local only per diagnostic_limits. Any aggregate win should be decomposed by target before synthesis, because a win driven only by the central segments must not be reported as uniform.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Numerical stability. Confirm that the explicit scheme satisfies the stability condition dt <= dx^2 / (2 k_max) for k up to 2.0, in both the generator and the physics forward model. Also confirm the treatment of the discontinuous k at segment interfaces (e.g. harmonic or arithmetic face averaging) is identical in both.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Validation reuse. This study supersedes S-Q1-01. Disclose whether the validation split informed any design choice here: physics iters or starts, baseline hyperparameters, or the 10% margin. If it did, these validation results are adaptively selected and should be labelled as such. Test and stress splits must remain untouched.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Fixed-configuration baselines. The MLP trains for 150 epochs with no early stopping and no tuning, and extra_trees is untuned. Synthesis must say the claim holds only against these specific configurations, not against tuned data-driven methods. The optional ridge arm should be reported only as context.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Synthesis framing. Any positive verdict must be stated as 'simulator access with an exact forward model (an inverse-crime setting) versus 3000 training rows'. It must not be stated as algorithmic superiority, and it must not be generalised to misspecified models, other noise levels, or other sensor layouts. Compute cost (forward solves versus training time) should be reported alongside accuracy, since compute is not matched.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Data-split integrity. Confirm that baseline training uses only the train split (fingerprint cdad...) with noise_aug=0. Confirm that the physics arm uses no training rows at all, so that the 'privileged factor' is only simulator access.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: No evidence exists. Status is 'planned', evidence_ids is empty, and verdicts is empty. No arm results, paired-bootstrap outputs or per-target diagnostics have been supplied. C-Q1-3 and C-Q1-4 cannot be assessed until all six required arms and the four required paired diagnostics (paired_et, paired_et_s1, paired_mlp, paired_mlp_s1) are produced on the validation split with the registered fingerprint edfcc32d…7c0543.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The claim structure does not match the claim text. Each claim object binds only treatment=S-Q1-03.physics and control=seed-0 arms, yet the text requires the margin at both seeds. The verdict rule must be stated explicitly. Recommended rule: both seed-0 and seed-1 paired diagnostics must have lower 95% bounds of 1 − relL2_T/relL2_C of at least 0.10. A seed-0-only pass must not be reported as a pass of either claim.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The bootstrap statistic is not defined. rel_l2 is a global Frobenius ratio, not a per-row mean, so the bootstrap must recompute ||P−Y||_F/||Y||_F for both arms on each resample. The procedure must use identical row indices for treatment and control and form the relative improvement 1 − T/C per resample. It must also specify the number of resamples (at least 2000), the CI method (percentile or BCa) and the RNG seed. A bootstrap of per-row errors or of a difference in means would not test the registered margin.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Row alignment must be verified. The diagnostics need evidence that physics and control predictions are joined on the same validation row identifiers in the same order, with no dropped rows. Physics rows that fail to converge or return NaN must be handled by a pre-declared rule, such as counting them as boundary or start-point predictions. Silently excluding them is not acceptable.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Implementation verification (required by both claims) must show that the estimator's forward model is identical to the data-generating simulator. This means the same 40-point grid, the same 200 explicit steps and dt, the same homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries, and the same Gaussian initial condition centred at 0.5. It also means the same treatment of the divergence-form flux at segment interfaces (for example, harmonic versus arithmetic averaging of k), the same sensor indices [5,15,25,35], and the same observation times and flatten order that produce the 80 features. A direct check is required: forward(true_k) for some validation rows must reproduce the noiseless signal to near machine precision, so residuals against the noisy observations should be on the order of 1e-3.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Stability (CFL) of the explicit finite-difference scheme must be checked at the upper bound k=2.0 and at every point the optimizer visits, including log-space excursions before clipping. If dt·k_max/dx² exceeds 0.5 anywhere in the search region, the likelihood surface is corrupted. This must be shown, not assumed.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The estimator specification is internally inconsistent. estimator='mode' with tikhonov=0 and a uniform prior implies a box-constrained MLE, but posterior_samples=128 is also listed. The implementation must state whether any sampling affects the reported point estimate. It must also state whether the log-space optimization adds a Jacobian or log-prior term: a mode in log k under a uniform prior on k differs from the MLE. Whether clipping is a projection on each iterate or only on the final value must be stated as well.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Leakage controls are needed for the physics arm. Multistart initial points must come from the seeded prior or a fixed design and must never come from validation targets. The noise sigma used in the likelihood must be the contract value 0.001, not an estimate from validation residuals. Iteration count, start count and any step-size settings must be fixed before validation results are viewed, since validation is a development split.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Optimizer adequacy must be reported. For each physics arm, report the fraction of rows that converge within 25 iterations, the distribution of final negative log-likelihood relative to its value at the true k, and the fraction of rows ending on the [0.5, 2.0] box boundary. Also report the total forward-evaluation count against the 3,000,000 budget. Without these, a failure cannot be attributed to the method rather than to under-iteration or local minima with only 3 starts.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The physics seed and control seed are not a matched pair in any causal sense. The physics seed changes only the start points; the control seed changes tree randomization or MLP initialization and batch order. Pairing in the bootstrap is over validation rows, not seeds. Synthesis must not describe seed 0 and seed 1 as matched replicates, and with n=2 it must make no statement about seed variance beyond the conjunctive pass or fail.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The controls are weak and fixed by design: untuned extra_trees, and an untuned MLP trained for 150 epochs with no early stopping that may overfit 3000 rows. The ridge arm is context only. Any positive result supports only the claim that the exact simulator beats these specific configurations. Synthesis must not generalize to 'physics beats data-driven methods', and must restate the inverse-crime and information-asymmetry qualifiers from the claim text.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Per-target diagnostics (required for ET and MLP) should report per-segment rel_l2 or RMSE for each arm. They should show whether any aggregate win is driven by the segments near the pulse centre (x≈0.5) while the outer segments are poorly identified. Local-Fisher results, if cited, must carry the contract caveat that they are local sensitivity only, not identifiability guarantees.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: A noise-floor context is needed for interpreting the margin. Report an oracle reference, such as the rel_l2 of the MLE initialized at the true k, or a CRLB-based expected error. This shows whether the ML baselines are already near the attainable floor, in which case a 10% margin may be infeasible regardless of method quality. This reference is for interpretation only and must not be used to adjust the verdict rule.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Multiplicity: the two claims are each conjunctive across seeds (an intersection-union test), so no correction is needed within a claim. However, reporting must not cherry-pick one claim or seed. Both claims must be reported together, with all four bounds, the point estimates, and any failures.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The held-out test and stress splits must not be touched. Evidence must confirm that only the train fingerprint (cdad48…a173) was used for fitting and only the val fingerprint was used for evaluation. The test fingerprint (aa0964…ed2c) must appear in no log for this study.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Fix and rerun the seed diagnostics S-Q1-02.paired_et_seed and S-Q1-02.paired_mlp_seed. Both failed with 'paired rows/seed/fidelity differ'. These diagnostics exist to vary the seed, but the claim-level allowed_varying_factors omit 'seed', even though the study-level matching allows it. The matcher therefore rejects them by construction. Add 'seed' to the allowed factors for these seed-spread diagnostics, or match them by row_hash and fidelity only. Both claims declare these diagnostics required, so C-Q1-1 and C-Q1-2 cannot leave 'inconclusive' until they succeed.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The reported intervals do not cover the uncertainty the claims require. The bootstrap intervals (ET relative effect [0.728, 0.770]; MLP [0.272, 0.352]) are explicitly 'row sampling conditional on fitted models; excludes training/task seed variation'. C-Q1-2 states that MLP seed-to-seed spread is folded into the uncertainty, and both claims set requires_uncertainty=true. Report an interval that combines row resampling with between-seed variance of the control, for example a nested or hierarchical bootstrap over seeds and rows. Judge the 0.10 margin against that combined interval.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Provide seed or restart variation for the physics treatment. Only seed 0 was run. The multistart initialisation (3 starts) is stochastic, and its sensitivity to the start seed is unmeasured. Run at least one additional physics seed, or show that the multistart is deterministic, and include it in the uncertainty.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Verify the implementation, as both claims require (requires_implementation_verification=true). Every arm has method_contract.diagnostics declared=[], observed=[], verified=false and source_hash=null. Export and certify artifacts, as the inference_policy requires, before any verdict is issued.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Provide evidence for the claim text's 'zero model misspecification (the forward operator equals the data generator)'. No artifact shows that the physics arm's forward solver matches the generator: same 40-point explicit FD grid, 200 steps, time step and stability condition, Gaussian IC at 0.5, Dirichlet BCs, sensor indices [5, 15, 25, 35], and segment-to-grid mapping. Supply a check that the physics forward map reproduces noise-free generator outputs to near machine precision on sample parameters.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Resolve the requested-versus-effective config change on every data-driven arm. noise_scale was requested as 0.0 but recorded as effective 1.0, and the requested and effective hashes differ. Show that noise_aug=0 makes noise_scale inert, so no augmentation copies were generated. The question explicitly specifies 'no noise augmentation'.
objections.author: critic-002
critic-002

objections.requirement: Reconcile the method description with its parameters. The text says 'box-clipped MLE under a uniform prior', while the params are estimator='mode', tikhonov=0.0 and posterior_samples=128. Confirm that posterior_samples is unused for the mode estimator. Confirm whether clipping is projection after the optimiser runs or a bounded optimiser in log space.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Report forward-evaluation usage for the physics arm on validation (750 rows × 3 starts × 25 iterations plus Jacobian evaluations) and confirm it stays within max_forward_evals=3,000,000.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Make the per-target diagnostics actually compare arms. S-Q1-02.per_target_physics_et and S-Q1-02.per_target_physics_mlp contain identical, treatment-only per_target_rel_l2 values and no control per-target rel_l2. Report control and treatment per-target rel_l2 side by side, with per-target paired intervals. The edge segments (targets 1 and 4, RMSE about 0.035) are notably worse than the interior segments; the synthesis should say whether the physics advantage holds for each segment.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Use more replicates. Two seeds per data-driven control give a one-degree-of-freedom spread estimate, and n_bootstrap=200 is thin for interval endpoints. Use at least 3–5 seeds and at least 1000 bootstrap resamples. Given the current lower bounds (0.27 and 0.73 against a 0.10 margin), this is unlikely to flip either claim, but it is needed for a credible seed-variance term.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Keep the synthesis within scope. The controls are fixed-configuration and untuned: extra_trees with max_features=0.5, and a 256x256 GELU MLP trained for 150 epochs. The test is an inverse-crime setting in which the inversion uses the exact generator and noise model, and the comparison is simulator access versus 3000 rows, not an equal-information comparison. Any conclusion must not generalise to 'physics methods outperform data-driven methods'. It must not imply robustness to model misspecification or transfer to the held-out test or stress splits.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Correct the completion bookkeeping. completion_fraction=1.0 and completed_work=5/5 are reported alongside status='incomplete', missing_diagnostics, and completed_claim_work=0/2. The completion metric should reflect the missing required diagnostics, so downstream synthesis does not treat the study as finished.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Document that the training observations carry the same noise process (i.i.d. N(0, 0.001²) per sensor) as the validation observations. Without this, part of the control gap could come from a train/validation noise mismatch rather than from simulator access.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Missing evidence: evidence_ids and verdicts are empty and status is 'planned'. C-Q2-1 cannot be evaluated until both required arms (S-Q2-01.mode, S-Q2-01.mean) have run on the same validation rows. Both required diagnostics (S-Q2-01.paired_mean_mode, S-Q2-01.per_target_mean_mode) must also be produced, with artifacts traceable to the val split fingerprint edfcc32d…7c0543.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Estimator definition (implementation): specify how 'posterior mean' is computed from the 128 posterior samples. Name the sampler (importance sampling from a Laplace/Gaussian proposal at the mode, MCMC, or other), the proposal, and the weighting. The mean must be taken in original conductivity space, i.e. E[k|y], not exp(E[log k|y]). Squared-error rel_l2 is minimized in expectation by the former. The latter is a geometric-mean/median-type estimator and would not test the stated hypothesis.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Prior/Jacobian correctness: the contract prior is i.i.d. uniform on [0.5, 2.0] in k, but sampling runs in log space (transform='log'). The target density in log k must include the Jacobian term (∝ k, i.e. +log k in the log-density) and must be truncated to [log 0.5, log 2]. If this is omitted, the sampler targets a log-uniform prior and the result is the posterior mean under the wrong prior. Verify this in code and with a unit test.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Likelihood correctness: the posterior must use additive i.i.d. Gaussian noise with sigma = 0.001 on all 80 features (4 sensors at indices [5,15,25,35] × 20 time samples). The same forward operator (40-point explicit FD, 200 steps, Dirichlet BCs, known Gaussian initial condition at x = 0.5) and the same time-subsampling as the data generator must be used. A mis-scaled sigma (e.g. one inflated by noise augmentation) changes posterior width and directly biases the mean-versus-mode gap.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Implementation verification (required by the claim): before reading validation results, validate the posterior-mean code on a toy case with a known posterior. Two options are a linear-Gaussian surrogate with an analytic mean, or a 1-parameter case checked by dense quadrature. Report the agreement. Also report importance-weight effective sample size (or MCMC diagnostics) per row. Rows with ESS near 1 make the 'mean' effectively equal to a single sample or the mode.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Matched control: confirm the mean arm reuses exactly the same multistart optimization as the mode arm. That means same 3 starts, 25 iterations, seed 0, and identical selected optimum per row, with only the final estimator differing. Also confirm the mode arm reproduces the values exported from S-Q1-03 bit-for-bit, or by a stated tolerance. A re-run that diverges from the S-Q1-03 export breaks the claimed 'identical settings' pairing.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Compute asymmetry: the mean arm spends at least 128 extra forward evaluations per row beyond the mode arm. Report forward-eval counts per arm. Confirm total usage across validation rows stays within max_forward_evals = 3,000,000, including multistart, gradient evaluations (adjoint or finite-difference) and posterior sampling. State whether the budget difference is accepted as part of the intervention.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Uncertainty specification: pre-register the paired bootstrap before looking at results. Fix the statistic as 1 − rel_l2(mean)/rel_l2(mode), with both global-Frobenius norms recomputed on the same resampled rows each replicate. Fix the number of replicates (≥ 2000), the interval method (percentile or BCa), the one-sided 95% lower bound, and the bootstrap RNG seed. The claim passes only if that lower bound is ≥ 0.02.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Unaccounted Monte Carlo variability: row-resampling uncertainty ignores sampler noise from the 128 posterior samples drawn under a single seed. Report the per-row Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior-mean estimate, or re-run the sampler with several seeds. This shows whether the improvement is stable relative to the 2% margin. Otherwise narrow the claim's scope explicitly to seed 0.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Optimizer convergence: 25 iterations with 3 starts may leave the mode arm unconverged on some rows. That would handicap the control and inflate the apparent benefit of averaging. Report per-row final objective, gradient norm or step size, the fraction of rows at a bound (clipping active), and the cross-start spread for both arms.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Numerical stability: explicit FD with k up to 2.0 must satisfy dt·k_max/dx² ≤ 0.5 for all parameters that posterior samples or optimizer iterates can reach. Specify the handling of NaN/unstable forward solves. Any failed rows must be identical across arms and reported, not silently dropped; dropping rows asymmetrically would bias the paired comparison.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Per-target diagnostic interpretation: report the rel_l2/RMSE difference per segment with paired uncertainty. A pooled 2% gain could be driven entirely by one poorly observed segment where the posterior is wide or bound-truncated. Link per-target gains to segment-sensor geometry rather than presenting them as a uniform improvement.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Training data isolation: state whether the training split (3000 rows, augmentation, scaler, PCA) influences either physics arm, e.g. via initialization or noise estimates. If it does, both arms must use it identically. Test and stress observations must not be used for any choice of sampler, proposal scale, sample count or margin.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Synthesis scope: the claim text must keep its stated limits. These are inverse-crime data (same simulator generated and inverts), single seed, row-resampling uncertainty only, and the validation split. It must not assert Bayes-optimality or global identifiability; per diagnostic_limits, any Fisher/Laplace argument is local only. Rename 'mode (MLE)' as 'box-clipped MLE (= MAP under the uniform prior with tikhonov = 0)' for precision.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Prior plausibility of the effect: with sigma = 0.001, posteriors may be very concentrated for well-observed segments, so mean ≈ mode there. A ≥ 2% pooled gain would then depend on weakly identified or boundary-truncated rows. Report posterior standard deviation (or Laplace width) per target alongside the result. A null outcome is then interpretable rather than attributed to implementation failure.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Implementation verification of the treatment branch: S-Q2-01 failed because 'posterior_mean' was silently normalised to 'mode'. Before any verdict, provide machine-checkable proof that the posterior-mean branch actually ran. This means the resolved estimator string logged per arm after harness normalisation, nonzero per-row prediction differences between the arms, and a posterior-sampling forward-eval count consistent with 128 samples per row. Identical or near-identical predictions must abort the comparison, not produce a 'no effect' result.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Specify the posterior-sampling algorithm for posterior_samples=128: Laplace/Gaussian approximation around the mode, MCMC, importance sampling, or prior sampling with reweighting. Report its diagnostics: acceptance rate or ESS, weight degeneracy, and the fraction of rows where samples collapse onto the mode. Without this, 'posterior mean' is undefined, and the estimand may just be a perturbed mode.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Prior/Jacobian correctness under transform='log'. The prior is uniform on k in [0.5, 2.0]. If sampling happens in log k, the density must include the Jacobian term exp(log k) and enforce the box truncation. Show that the target density used by the sampler matches the stated posterior: uniform-on-k prior times Gaussian likelihood with sigma=0.001.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Define the space in which the mean is taken. Under squared error on k, the rel_l2-relevant estimator is E[k|y]. exp(E[log k|y]) is a geometric-mean estimator, which is a different intervention. The output must be the sample average of k in original units, after the inverse transform per sample and not after averaging.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Mode-arm convergence evidence. With 25 iterations and 3 starts, report per-row final data misfit for both arms, e.g. the chi-square of the residuals against 80 * sigma^2. Also report the fraction of rows at box bounds and the fraction of non-converged rows. If posterior_mean improves mainly on rows where the mode optimiser failed, the effect is optimiser repair, not estimator choice. The claim must be stratified by convergence status.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Matched control audit. Confirm that both arms use identical multistart initial points and identical optimiser trajectories up to the point where sampling begins; seed 0 must yield the same start draws. Confirm that the posterior_mean arm does not receive extra optimisation iterations or starts beyond the sampler budget. List every config field that differs between the arms; only params.estimator may differ.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Clarify 'box-clipped mode = MAP'. Post-hoc clipping of an unconstrained log-space optimum is not the constrained maximiser of the posterior. Either show that the constrained optimum is used, or report the fraction of rows where clipping is active and drop the MAP equivalence wording in the synthesis.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Pre-specify the paired bootstrap. State the number of resamples (e.g. B >= 2000), the bootstrap RNG seed, and the interval method (percentile vs BCa). Use joint row resampling of both arms, recompute both Frobenius norms per resample, and use the one-sided lower bound on the ratio statistic 1 - rel_l2(pm)/rel_l2(mode) compared against the 0.02 margin. Report the point estimate, the bound and the full bootstrap distribution summary.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Monte Carlo variability of the 128-sample estimator is not captured by row resampling. At minimum, report a sensitivity check: re-run the posterior_mean arm with different sampler seeds, or a subset of rows with posterior_samples=512. This shows that the margin is not an artefact of a single sampler seed. The claim's scope statement should explicitly exclude sampler-seed variance if this is not done.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Required per-target diagnostic (S-Q2-02.per_target_pm_mode). Report per-target rel_l2/RMSE for both arms with paired intervals. The global Frobenius metric can be dominated by one poorly identified segment, e.g. a segment far from sensors or near the boundaries. The synthesis must state whether the gain is concentrated in a subset of targets.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Effect plausibility and identifiability context. With sigma=0.001 and 80 observations, the posterior may be very concentrated for most rows, so posterior mean ≈ mode. Report posterior spread per target, e.g. the 128-sample std relative to the prior range, together with local Fisher-based standard errors. This lets readers interpret a null or positive result. The contract limits these to local sensitivity only, so no global identifiability claim may be made from them.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Forward-evaluation budget accounting. Report total forward evaluations per arm: 750 rows × 3 starts × 25 iterations × gradient cost, plus sampler cost. Confirm the total is within the 3,000,000 cap. Confirm that any budget-exhausted rows are flagged rather than silently returning the initial point or the mode.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Numerical stability of the explicit finite-difference forward model. Verify the CFL condition dt*k_max/dx^2 <= 0.5 at k=2.0 with 40 points and 200 steps. Also verify that sampler or optimiser proposals outside [0.5, 2.0] are rejected before simulation, since unstable forward solves would corrupt likelihoods. Report any NaN/inf counts per arm.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Data provenance. Confirm that both arms were evaluated on exactly the 750 validation rows matching fingerprint edfcc32d..., in the same row order. Confirm that the test split (fingerprint aa0964...) was not loaded or inspected. Note that the training split, noise augmentation, scaler and PCA stages in transform_order do not apply to this physics estimator; confirm none of them silently altered the inputs.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Missing evidence. evidence_ids is empty and dependency S-Q1-03 has no recorded status in this artifact. No verdict on C-Q2-2 can be issued until the run artifacts and the dependency's outcome are attached: per-row predictions for both arms, resolved configs, the bootstrap output and the required diagnostics.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Synthesis scope discipline. Any conclusion must keep the stated scope: inverse crime/zero misspecification, simulator access, single seed, row-resampling uncertainty only, development split. It must not generalise to misspecified models, other noise levels or held-out performance, and must make no Bayes-optimality claim. If the lower bound falls below 0.02, the result must be reported as 'not supported at the margin' even if the point estimate exceeds it.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The treatment arm must actually run the posterior-mean estimator. Arm S-Q2-01.mean requested estimator='mean', which is not in the allowed set ['mode', 'posterior_mean']. It was silently normalized to 'mode' (see the normalization_changes note and the gate note 'using default'). Its effective_hash d9bed87f… is identical to the control's effective_hash. This study therefore compared the MLE with itself. Re-register the treatment with estimator='posterior_mean', confirm that its effective_hash differs from the control's, and re-run.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Retract or void the verdict 'contradicted' for C-Q2-1. The effect is exactly 0.0 with interval [0.0, 0.0]. The per-sample squared errors, the per-target RMSE and the summary statistics are identical across arms. Both arms cite the same evidence artifact (resu-00297 appears twice in source_artifacts and evidence_ids). This shows the arms are identical, not that posterior-mean failed to improve on the MLE. The correct status is 'invalid / not tested', not 'contradicted'.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The gate and matching checks must reject arms whose requested and effective method contracts differ in the varied factor. Gate-00293 approved the arm with method_valid=true despite a normalization change on params.estimator. That parameter is the only allowed varying factor, so the arm violates the study's own matching design. The matching_issues list is empty, which is incorrect. Add a check that fails when allowed_varying_factors resolve to identical effective values across arms.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Each arm must produce its own result artifact. Both arms resolve to resu-00297. The paired diagnostic needs distinct control and treatment artifacts, plus row_hash matching, to count as a paired comparison.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement:
Implementation verification is required by the claim (requires_implementation_verification=true), but it is missing. method_contract.diagnostics shows declared=[], observed=[], verified=false for both arms. Provide evidence that the posterior-mean path works as intended:
- It draws the 128 posterior samples.
- It uses the stated likelihood (sigma=0.001) and the uniform [0.5, 2.0]^4 prior.
- It returns something other than the mode.

One example is a unit test on a synthetic case where the mean and mode differ analytically.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Specify how the posterior mean is computed relative to the log transform. Averaging samples in log-k and then exponentiating gives the posterior geometric mean, not E[k | data]. Under the squared-error metric rel_l2, only E[k | data] is Bayes-optimal. The claim's justification depends on which one is computed. Declare this, and preferably average in the original k space.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement:
Characterize the posterior sampler before attributing any effect to the estimator. Report:
- the sampler type, burn-in and acceptance rate
- convergence diagnostics such as ESS or R-hat
- the Monte Carlo standard error of the 128-sample mean relative to the 2% margin
- how the samples respect the box prior (rejection, reflection or clipping)

Clipping or reflecting at the bounds would bias the mean.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Describe the control accurately. The claim calls it a 'box-clipped mode (MLE)'. With a uniform prior and tikhonov=0, the MAP equals the box-constrained MLE only if the optimizer enforces the box rather than clipping after the fact. Document which it does, because post-hoc clipping changes the estimator and could favour either arm.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: The uncertainty does not support a general claim. It uses a single seed, row-bootstrap only, and n_bootstrap=200, which is coarse for a lower 95% bound. Multistart initialization and posterior sampling are stochastic, so the treatment needs seed replication across at least several seeds. Either use more bootstrap resamples or use a BCa or percentile interval with the number of resamples reported.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Scope the synthesis claims to their conditions. The setting is an inverse crime: the same 40-point, 200-step explicit simulator generates and inverts the data, with known initial condition and noise model. A posterior-mean advantage under these conditions does not transfer to misspecified models. The 'zero model misspecification' caveat must be carried into any downstream conclusion.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Report per-target effects in the re-run. The end segments (targets 1 and 4) have about 5x the RMSE of the interior segments (0.036 vs 0.007). This is consistent with weaker sensitivity near the Dirichlet boundaries, where posterior spread and mode–mean divergence should be largest. Any aggregate effect should be broken down by target, ideally with a local-Fisher or posterior-width diagnostic per segment. Interpret that diagnostic within its stated local-only limits.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Remove the duplicated diagnostics. S-Q2-01.per_sample_mean_mode (resu-00301) and S-Q2-01.per_target_mean_mode (resu-00300) contain identical payloads, and each reports only one set of values with no control/treatment split. Each diagnostic should report both arms separately so that it can detect arm identity.
objections.author: critic-002

objections.requirement: Confirm data hygiene for the re-run. Test and stress splits must not be consulted. The validation rows (row_hash 260db427…) must match across arms. No tuning of posterior_samples, iters or multistart may be based on validation outcomes from this comparison.
objections.author: critic-002

messages.author: researcher-003
messages.question: Q-1
messages.text: Design rationale, not a result: no evidence exists yet, so every claim here is an untested hypothesis. The forward map is deterministic, has 4 parameters, and the noise is small (sigma=1e-3). Under those conditions, likelihood-based fitting through the simulator should approach the local noise floor. Regressors trained on 3000 prior samples face an 80-dimensional input and are limited by sample density. The margin is a 10% relative improvement, not 'any' improvement, so that a 'substantially lower' finding means something. Both strong library controls use log targets, matching the physics log transform, so the comparison isolates estimator class rather than parameterization. Ridge is an optional linear floor. The physics settings (25 iters, 3 starts) are chosen to fit the 760 s budget, and forward-eval usage should stay far below the 3M cap. If physics wins by less than the margin, or the paired diagnostic shows a heavy tail of multistart failures, the next step is the hybrid initializer from Q-2 rather than more starts. The per-target diagnostic is collected now so Q-3 can reuse it. The claims are not certified here; they need the executed paired diagnostics and implementation verification.

interpretation.interpretation: Task task-001 (artifact resu-00129, specialist-004) did not produce any diagnostic output. The task status is 'incomplete' and the result status is 'unsupported', with the stated uncertainty 'no executable study returned'. The run used 38.0 s of a 60 s limit. No numbers exist for any of the requested quantities: (a) chi2(estimate) vs chi2(truth) optimizer-failure fraction and chi2(estimate)/80 distribution, (b) per-target bound-hit fractions at 0.5 / 2.0, (c) non-finite and fallback counts, (d) median Cramér–Rao standard deviations from the local Fisher information at true k. Q-1 therefore gets no new evidence on optimizer adequacy or clipping for the physics arm of S-Q1-02 (resu-00118, val_pred at exp-0007). Any earlier interpretation of that arm's errors as optimizer failure, bound clipping, or intrinsic non-identifiability stays unresolved by this task. The null result is not evidence for or against any of these hypotheses. The failure is in execution or tooling: no study was returned. That differs from a finding that the diagnostic is infeasible. The request was within budget (about 3,300 forward evals) and used validation rows only. Suggested next step: resubmit as an executable script using batched forward calls, or split the request into (a–c), which need only the stored predictions plus 2 evals per row, and (d), which runs on 200 rows.

messages.author: researcher-003
messages.question: Q-1
messages.text:
Researcher interpretation (unverified; no claim is certified). S-Q1-02 executed all 5 required arms on the same 750 validation rows (row_hash 260db427…). Both claims are still inconclusive. The only unmet requirements are the two seed diagnostics, S-Q1-02.paired_et_seed and S-Q1-02.paired_mlp_seed. They failed with 'paired rows/seed/fidelity differ' because they pair arms with different seeds, which the harness's paired analysis does not allow. This is a design error on my part, not a result.

Measured values (validation rel_l2, original k scale per the harness metric):
- physics: 0.01933
- extra_trees: 0.07741 (s0), 0.07711 (s1)
- torch_mlp: 0.02805 (s0), 0.03016 (s1)
- ridge (context only, per obj-015): 0.06603

Paired bootstrap results (200 resamples, row sampling only, conditional on fitted models):
- physics vs ET s0: relative improvement 0.750, 95% interval [0.728, 0.770] (resu-00120).
- physics vs MLP s0: relative improvement 0.311, 95% interval [0.272, 0.352] (resu-00121).
- Both lower bounds exceed the 0.10 margin.

Under the pre-registered conservative rule (each claim must hold against the better-scoring control seed):
- The better MLP seed is s0, which is already the paired control.
- For ET, the better seed is s1. The point estimate against it is 1 − 0.01933/0.07711 ≈ 0.749. That figure is my arithmetic, not a paired artifact.

Caveats that remain open:
1. Seed variance is unestimated with 2 seeds (obj-020), and the physics arm is single-seed (obj-021).
2. torch_mlp_s1 (resu-00110) and ridge (resu-00111) are cache reuses of earlier experiments (exp-0005, exp-0006); torch_mlp_s1 ran on cpu. That the seed-1 intervention was actually applied is not verified (intervention_verified=false on all arms).
3. Optimizer adequacy is not yet shown (obj-018). last_iters=25 equals the cap on at least the last row, and no per-row NLL(estimate) vs NLL(truth) or convergence data exists.
4. Boundary-clipping fractions are not reported (obj-025).
5. n_bootstrap=200 is small for the interval tails.

Partial evidence on earlier objections:
- Inverse-crime and fidelity (obj-002): fit_report shows residual_std_at_truth 0.000995 ≈ sigma, model_mismatch=false, and last chi2/dof 0.963. This points to an exact forward model, so any win must be framed as simulator access in an inverse-crime setting (obj-030).
- Forward-eval budget (obj-023): 174,077 total evals (about 232 per row plus 200 in fit), against a 3,000,000 cap.
- Compute is not matched (obj-010): physics predicts in 14.95 s at about 19.9 ms per row; MLP takes 10.2 s to fit and about 0.016 ms per row to predict.
- Uncertainty calibration: 1σ/2σ coverage is 0.702/0.957, close to nominal.

Per-target pattern, relevant to Q-3 and obj-026:
- physics per-target rel_l2: [0.0268, 0.0060, 0.0050, 0.0263]. The outer segments k1 and k4 are about 4–5× worse than the central ones.
- ET and MLP show the same outer/inner ordering.
- Physics is lower than ET and MLP on every target (per-target RMSE in resu-00120/121). The aggregate win is therefore not driven only by the central segments, though it is smallest in relative terms for MLP on k4 (0.0350 vs 0.0448 RMSE).
- Ridge's central-segment errors (0.0128, 0.0113) beat both nonlinear baselines there. This suggests the central map is close to linear, and that the baseline weakness is concentrated in the outer segments.

Next step: revise to S-Q1-03 so that the seed requirement is satisfiable through matched-seed pairs. This adds a physics seed-1 arm, which also addresses obj-021, at an estimated ~17 s. In parallel, commission the optimizer-adequacy and clipping diagnostic.
